title: LandlordGuard Vacancy Permit Day-Count Convention
content:
This convention sets how the charged permit days of a vacancy permit on the LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy are counted. It turns on how long the building has already stood vacant on the permit start, counting the vacancy start date as day 1.

**Convention.**

- A building vacant more than the tier's vacancy exclusion period (60 days on every LandlordGuard tier) is charged in whole 30-day blocks: the permit days rounded up to the next multiple of 30.
- A building vacant more than 30 days but not more than 60 days is charged in whole 7-day weeks: the permit days rounded up to the next multiple of 7.
- A building vacant 30 days or fewer is charged for the permit days themselves.

A number of permit days that is already a multiple of 30 or of 7 stays as it is under the matching rule.

## Days vacant on the permit start

The days vacant are counted from the vacancy start date on the policy, as day 1, through the permit start. A building whose vacancy start date is 1 April has stood vacant 61 days on 31 May and 60 days on 30 May.

## Input — judgement — charged days (hypothetical permits)

| Days vacant on the permit start | Permit days | Rule | Charged permit days |
|---|---|---|---|
| 61 | 45 | 30-day blocks | 60 |
| 60 | 45 | 7-day weeks | 49 |
| 31 | 45 | 7-day weeks | 49 |
| 30 | 45 | the permit days | 45 |
| 75 | 90 | 30-day blocks | 90 |
| 45 | 41 | 7-day weeks | 42 |
| 10 | 41 | the permit days | 41 |

The charged permit days are the day count used in the permit charge; the permit's own first and last day are unchanged by this convention.
